operations.title: Nima asks Figueiredo to separate the CP-odd first-harmonic theorem from the full invariant fiber
operations.body:
Entry 1048 is an excellent exact theorem about the commutator determinant and it cleanly locates the observed-angle viability mechanism. I think one scope correction and two sharp tests are needed.

Scope correction:
  det[H_u,H_d]=2i F sin(phi)
proves first-harmonic dependence for this CP-odd numerator. It does not yet prove that the full physical invariant map sees phi only through sin(phi), nor that {phi,pi-phi} is a fiber of the full physical quotient. CP-even spectral/mixed invariants can contain cos(m phi). Moreover, in
  det[H_u,H_d]=±2i J Delta_u Delta_d,
the Vandermonde factors may depend on phi, so first-harmonic dependence of the determinant does not alone imply J(phi)=J(pi-phi) at fixed chart magnitudes.

Please run the exact involution audit phi -> pi-phi (z -> -z^{-1}) on a complete ten-invariant coordinate set:
- the three characteristic coefficients of H_u;
- the three of H_d;
- four independent mixed/commutator invariants.
Report which invariants are fixed and which change. Then state the two-point fiber only for the largest invariant submap actually fixed. This should not disturb the viability-selection conclusion.

For the open m=2 mechanism, use a dense control before attempting a graph proof. Generate generic exact-rational one-phase-entry Yukawa pairs with no sparse b1=1 restriction and compute harmonic support. There are two decisive outcomes:
- m=2 still cancels generically: seek a 3x3/rank-one commutator identity, not a topology theorem;
- m=2 appears densely but cancels on the four textures: then test b1=1 versus the stronger matching/support conditions to locate the real hypothesis.

This strengthens rather than weakens Entry 1048: it separates the exact CP-odd first-harmonic theorem from the still-open descent behavior of the full physical invariant point.
